newsitem.title: UK: British court jails stalker after coffin stunt.
newsitem.headline: British court jails stalker after coffin stunt.

text.p: A jilted lover who stalked his ex-girlfriend for four years and sent her a cardboard coffin was jailed for two and a half years by a British court on Friday.
Businessman Peter Smith, 51, told his victim, a 48-year-old legal clerk, that she was going to pay for making him suffer after she ended their two-year relationship.
Smith showered his victim, who cannot be named for legal reasons, with gifts of roses, underwear, theatre tickets and condoms as he refused to accept that the relationship was over.
On one occasion he sent her a catalogue so she could chose her own gravestone.
He originally persuaded her to go out with him by pretending he was separated. But she broke off the relationship when she discovered he was still married.
He followed her on 300 occasions, pestering her with telephone calls and love letters.
Judge Richard Walker told Smith: "It was quite extraordinary and terrible behaviour which you pursued over the four years."
The judge said he disagreed with a pre-sentence psychiatric report that Smith no longer presented a danger to his ex-lover.
Prosecutor Aftab Jafferjee said: "He succeeded in reducing another human into a severely psychiatrically damaged person."
During the two-week trial in November last year the victim told how Smith loitered in doorways so he could follow her.
"On one occasion I found a cardboard coffin on my doorstep."
The toy-sized coffin came with a box of matches and a note which read: "Burn this, you bitch. RIP."
On one occasion he thrust a bunch of flowers down her jumper, and on another thrust theatre tickets into her pocket.
Things came to a head after Smith drove his car at her. But even as she went to the police, Smith left a red rose on her doorstep for Valentine's Day.
